findings.rationale: SRC-TRIAGE-006-ADR-A (REQ-TRIAGE-006-A) requires evaluated_at <= deadline (inclusive), while SRC-TRIAGE-006-ADR-B (REQ-TRIAGE-006-B) requires evaluated_at < deadline (exclusive). Both sources are ACTIVE, have equal authority (architecture_contract), identical scope, and neither supersedes the other. No repository governance resolves the conflict. The implementation uses strict-less-than (<), which satisfies REQ-TRIAGE-006-B but violates REQ-TRIAGE-006-A. Because the authoritative sources are irreconcilably in conflict for an in-scope, deadline/boundary-critical requirement, SOURCE_CONFLICT applies as the most-specific finding type under domain_rules_v1.0.yaml. The tests do not exercise the evaluated_at == deadline boundary, so correctness of the boundary cannot be verified regardless of which requirement is authoritative. Per DR-003 and advisory_resolution precedence, an unresolved in-scope authoritative source conflict mandates ABSTAIN.
findings.suggested_human_check: Determine which of REQ-TRIAGE-006-A (<=) and REQ-TRIAGE-006-B (<) is the authoritative deadline boundary operator, record an explicit supersession in sources.yaml, then re-verify. Also add a test case for evaluated_at == deadline once the boundary is resolved.
